newsitem.title: USA: Delaware Otsego says in talks with CSX, Norfolk.
newsitem.headline: Delaware Otsego says in talks with CSX, Norfolk.

text.p: Money-losing freight railroad Delaware Otsego Corp. said Wednesday it is in discussions to be acquired by Norfolk Southern Corp. and CSX Corp.

In a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Delaware Otsego President Walter Rich said talks with the two railroads have already taken place in conjunction with their proposed joint acquisition of East Coast railroad Conrail Inc. by CSX and Norfolk.
CSX and Norfolk agreed in April to buy Conrail for $10.3 billion. The takeover plan must be approved by federal regulators.

Rich, who holds the equivalent of a 14.9 percent stake in Delaware Otsego, said the talks are expected to continue about the "possiblity of participating in a transaction involving the acquisition of the company or certain assets."

Rich's latest disclosure came a day after CSX Corp., which holds a 6 percent stake in Delaware Otsego, confirmed in a separate SEC filing that it was considering the "possibility of participating with others" in the acquisition of Delaware Otsego.
Delaware Otsego operates a 500-mile freight railroad network in New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania.
The railroad has lost money in five of the last eight quarters. In the first quarter of 1997, it lost $691,000, or 38 cents a share.

The company's stock rose $1.25 to $22 in trading on Nasdaq Wednesday. Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern's stock slipped 19 cents to $111.125 and Richmond, Va.-based CSX rose 50 cents to $60.69, both in composite trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
